saints.name: The Four Crowned Martyrs
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: Roman martyrs of the Diocletian persecution honoured on the Caelian Hill from the earliest centuries…
biography: The Quattuor Coronati are among the most anciently venerated martyrs of Rome, commemorated on the Caelian Hill where the basilica of the Santi Quattro Coronati still stands. Their traditions are intertwined: one names four soldiers or officials put to death under Diocletian for refusing to worship the pagan god Aesculapius.

A second account, joined to their feast, honours a group of Pannonian stonemasons — Claudius, Nicostratus, Symphorian, Castorius, and Simplicius — who suffered death rather than carve an idol for the emperor. Whatever the exact history behind the names, their cult in Rome is very old, and they were long invoked as patrons of sculptors and stonemasons.
saints.knownFor: Ancient Roman martyrs venerated as patrons of stonemasons.
